senses.gloss: , fut. יֵימָא, imper. אֵימָא (√אם to join, v. אמר) to say, speak, think.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 33:10">Targ. Y. Gen. XXXIII, 10</cite>.—Freq. in Talmud.—<he>אפילו תימא</he> even if you will say, i.e. it may come right even if you assume that &c.
Succ. 13ᵇ; a. fr.—מי לֵימָא, (מי)נֵימָא, or לימא must it be said, does it mean to say? Ib.; a. fr.—(ואי) וכי תימא and if you should object.
<cite ref="Sukkah 13b:1">Ib.</cite>; a. fr.—<he>אלא אימא</he> but rather say, i.e. the correct version is.

<cite ref="Sukkah 13b:1">Ib.</cite>; a. fr.—<he>אימא סיפא</he> now read the second clause, i.e. how will you understand &c.? <cite ref="Berakhot 21b:1">Ber. 21ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>אֵימָא</he> I might think.
<cite ref="Berakhot 21b:1">Ib.</cite>; a. fr.—<he>הוה אמינא</he> I might have thought, I might have been led to believe.

<cite ref="Eruvin 74b:5-6">Erub. 74ᵇ</cite> <he>מאי הוה א׳</he> what might I have been led to believe?; a. fr.—<he>נימא כוותיה</he> let him express his opinion in agreement with his authority, i.e. why does he not say so expressly? <cite ref="Taanit 3a:7">Taan. 3ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—
Pes. 7ᵇ היכי נימא what else should he say? נימא למול should he use the expression lamol?—
<cite ref="Gittin 47b">Gitt. 47ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>ס״ד אמינא</he> it may occur to you to think; v. <cite ref="D00951"><he>דַּעְתָּא</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Yoma 85b:3">Yoma 85ᵇ</cite> <he>אי הואי התם הוה אמינא</he> had I been there, I should have said.—<he>קאמינא</he> = <he>קא אמינא</he> I say, speak of, v. <cite ref="S00003"><he>קָא</he></cite>.
